For the quadratic equation $2x^2 + 3kx + k = 0$ to have two distinct real roots, its discriminant must be strictly positive:
$$\Delta = b^2 - 4ac > 0$$
$$(3k)^2 - 4(2)(k) > 0 \implies 9k^2 - 8k > 0$$

State the outside solution intervals:
$$k < 0 \quad \text{or} \quad k > \frac{8}{9} \quad \left(\text{or } (-\infty, 0) \cup \left(\frac{8}{9}, \infty\right)\right)$$
